### EEN EN DERTIGSTE HOOFDSTUK.
### De Zee-Handschoen.

Dit is ook een spongieus gewas, uit een smal begin zig ver uitbreidende in veele vingeren, beneden smal, en allegaar by malkander gevoegt, boven breed, en met een gat, voorts binnen bol, van tweederlei gedaante.

De eerste heeft veele ronde vingeren, sommige niet dikker, dan een duim, boven met een smal rond gaatje.

Andere zyn zoo dik als een kinder arm, en wyd geopent als een darm. Voorts binnen bol als een bekertje, of gelyk afgesneede vingeren aan de wolle handschoen, binnen effener dan buiten, van substantie als wol en spongie door malkander gemengt, van couleur vaal-graauw als andere spongie.

Het staat zonder kennelyke wortelen op alderhande klippen, en in de bolligheden van de vingeren woonen kleine Visjes en Garnaaltjes, daar uit en inzwemmende.

De tweede gedaante heeft langere en boven spitzere vingeren, van buiten heel steekelig, dog de doorens zyn niet hard, grover en breeder van geweef dan het voorgaande, meer na de spongieuse dan boute natuur trekkende. Binnen zyn de vingeren mede bol en effen, daar diergelyke Visjes en Garnaaltjes in speelen. Het zyn bossen ruim een voet hoog, met veele vingeren nevens malkander gewassen, op een slegten wortel staande.

Naam. In 't Latyn *Chirotheca marina*; in 't Maleits *Sarong tangan laut*.

Plaats en Gebruik. Deze gewassen dienen tot niets, maar werden gelyk het voorgaande tot rariteit bewaart.

In deze Chirotheca marina woont een ander klein Visje van een byzondere aart en fatzoen, een slag van *Ican batu*, plat en dun, rood met zwartagtige banden, die men ook onder de bolle steenen vindt, hy woont in deze vingeren, maar men weet egter niet, dat hy dezelve formeerd, hy pikt na de menschen als een Hoen, als men hem te na komt, dog zonder zeer te doen.

---

### TWEE EN DERTIGSTE HOOFDSTUK.
### De Zee-Baart.

Daar volgen nog twee zeldzame zeegewassen, die met de Zoophytis ook al mede gemeenschap hebben, dog de steenige natuur nog al nader zyn, en dierhalven in dit Boek behooren.

1. *Barba marina* schynt een bondeltje te zyn, van witte of gryze, styve borsteltjes, in gedaante van een quast of groffe Pinceel. Beneden staan ze op een knobbelagtige wortel, geformeert schier als een klootzak, gemaakt van klein en steenig gruis. Hier in steeken de borstels, zynde de geheele quast ruim een span lank, boven spits toeloopende gelyk een kegel, van buiten effen, en wat boekig, omgeven met een fyne substantie, gelyk het linnen *Tsjavony* genaamt, daar onder men veele oogjes of gaatjes ziet. Dit steenagtig linnen afgetrokken zynde, vertoonen baar eerst de witte of gryze borstels in de dikte van Paardsbairen, ruig en scherp, inzonderheid omtrent het onderste, daar ze ook eenigzints snyden. Als dan open hun de bairen des kegels, en maken een verwerden baart, in 't aanraken ligt breekende, en de stukken kleeven aan de huid met een klein jeuken. De rest van de keegel kleeft nog al aan malkander gelyk een lok bairs, die door vuiligheid en neeten aan malkander hangt. Onder water schynt het met zyn slymerig vel eenig gevoelen te vertoonen, maar boven water kan men geen teeken van leven nog beweeging daar aan gewaar werden, behalven een klein jeuken op de huid.

Naam. In 't Latyn *Barba marina*; in 't Maleits mag men 't noemen *Djangot* of *Barba laut*. By anderen werd het ook *Penicillus marinus* genaamt, want een gedaante daar van ook in de Middellandsche Zee gevonden werd. Hier te lande komt het zelden voor den dag, werdende maar somtyts opgehaalt met de Vissers boeken, die wat diep in zee gelaten werden. Het heeft ook tot nog toe geen bekent gebruik, want de Vissers houden 't voor een schadelyk gewas, smytende het straks weder in zee.

The falling rain is also repeated in many other works, conspicuously, for example, in the late Kāṅgrā example of Plate LVIII. The lightning of most of the late Kāṅgrā paintings (Plates LVIII, LXXI, B, LXXIII, A) is, however, much more realistic, and so with the clouds (Plate LV).

The suggestion of Far-Eastern art in the Bikāner mural fragment is one that occasionally becomes conspicuous in Rājasthānī art,¹ particularly at Bikāner, where true Chinese clouds are painted on the lacquered shields, and at Udaipur, where the wall-painting of the island palaces, perhaps by an 18th century hand, evidently repeats a Chinese model. Amongst Pahāṛī drawings, also, one occasionally meets with a copy of some Chinese motif. The Chinese element in Rājput art, however, is purely sporadic, and cannot be traced as an integral factor, as it became in Persian painting, and to a smaller extent also in Mughal. In Rājput art I am inclined to trace the Chinese motifs to the sea-borne commerce. There has long existed an extensive importation of Chinese embroidery into Gujarāt, and this is still continued, while fragments of Chinese embroidery several centuries old are often to be met with in Western India, associated with purely Indian work.

The most familiar Rājasthānī painting is that of Jaipur in the 18th century.² Its most impressive examples are the large cartoons represented on Plates IX and X, which are selected from a number of the working drawings (mostly pricked for reproduction by pouncing) designed for two large paintings on cloth now preserved in the library of the Mahārājā of Jaipur, and probably executed in the latter part of the 18th century. In these works, and another large picture reproduced on Plate XI, we see the persistence of ancient art, not merely in a miniature adaptation, but on its true scale.³ These large works are in the purest idiom of Hindū art, handed down from century to century, with a certainty and loyalty which is only paralleled in the transmission of the sacred texts. We wonder at the persistence of tradition in the art of Egypt; it is scarcely less remarkable that the Hindūs, through centuries of religious evolution and of warfare should have been able to preserve almost to our own time so much of the grandeur that belongs to the art of the period of their supreme achievement.⁴ These works alone are sufficient proof of the authentic and autochthonous character of Rājput painting.

These works are an immediate expression of the Hindū view of life. Here is that distinct, sharp and wiry bounding line which Blake, most Indian of modern Western minds, regarded as the golden rule of art and life. A line so deliberate, so self-confident, so full of wonder at the beauty of the world, especially the beauty of women, and at the same time so austere, could not be a sudden achievement, nor depend on the brilliance of a single personality. It is the product of a whole civilization, and of aristocratic traditions protected by hieratic sanctions. In this work there is no room for cleverness; too haughty to admire ingenuity, too distinguished to affect a calligraphic elegance, or to feel the smallest interest in any attempt to create an illusion of modelling, it is an art both proud and passionate and very reserved. It is sometimes said that the Indians have left no history; but what else than history is any work of traditional art? Of such art we can at least say that it is not a product of chance, but is determined by antecedent racial *karma*, and cannot

As regards the warmth: evil spirits also can by their artifices produce a warmth which counterfeits delight, and can communicate it to others; but it is only an external warmth, without an origin from internals. Such warmth is that which putrefies and converts food into excrement, like the heat of adulterers, and that of those who have been immersed in filthy pleasures.

**1774.** There are spirits who do not desire to hear anything about the interior things of the Word; and even should they understand them, they are still unwilling. They are chiefly those who have placed merit in works, and who therefore have done goods from the love of self and of the world, or for the sake of the rank or wealth to be gained for themselves, and the consequent reputation, thus not for the sake of the Lord's kingdom. In the other life such desire more than others to enter heaven; but they remain outside of it; for they are unwilling to be imbued with the knowledges of truth, and thereby to be affected with good. They interpret the meaning of the Word from the letter according to their fancies, and by advancing whatever favors their cupidities with its approval. Such were represented by an old woman who had a face not comely, but of even snowy paleness, with irregular features (*cui inerant inordinata*), which made her ugly. But those who admit and love the interior things of the Word, were represented by a girl in early maidenhood, or in the flower of youth, handsomely dressed, and adorned with garlands and heavenly ornaments.

**1775.** I have conversed with certain spirits concerning the Word, saying that it has been necessary that of the Lord's Divine Providence some revelation should come into existence, for a revelation or Word is the general recipient vessel of spiritual and celestial things, thus conjoining heaven and earth; and that without it they would have been disjoined, and the human race would have perished. Ad secundum gradum dicendum quod secundum philosophum in quarto ethicorum omnia illa quorum precium numismate potest comparari vel censeri potest in re dati et accepti venire: et ideo illi actus qui in subuentionem aliene miserie exhibentur etiam quando dona accipiuntur cum sine precio impenduntur. Ad tertium dicendum quod habitus distinguitur ex actibus et actus ex obiectis: ideo quandoque nomina equiuocantur ad habitus actus et obiecta: sicut patet de fide: quae potest significare vel habitum fidei vel actum eius aut ipsam rem creditam. Et similiter elemosine nomen aliquando significat ipsam rem datam et sic non diffinitur hic. Aliquando ipsam dationem et sic accipitur predicta diffinitio. Ad quartum dicendum quod clerici etiam si ipsi non indigeant elemosine dantur ut ministris pauperum et dispensatoribus elemosinarum: et ideo quod eis in elemosinam datur per eos pauperibus transmittitur. Ad quintum dicendum quod sicut in libro distinctione vigesimasexta dicitum est: nomina passionum sensibilium aliquando per quandam similitudinem transferuntur ad actus voluntatis qui sine passione sunt: et sic compassio quae proprie importat passionem tristitiae de aliena miseria de qua de ipso actu voluntatis quo alicui displicet aliena miseria: et sine tali compassione nunquam elemosina danda est: quia non subueniret aliquis miserie aliene nisi vellet eum non esse miserum: et talis compassio etiam in deo est: quia ei mala nostra: ex voluptate antecedente displicent: et quicquid etiam ex parte nostri in nobis etiam quandoque adiungitur compassio proprie dicta: quia appetitus superior natus est appetitum inferiorem mouere: unde si sit fortis impressio in superiori: erit etiam in inferiori nisi aliquid repugnet: et secundum hoc misericordia et verecundia et quedam alie passiones laudabiles sunt inquantum ex debita electione boni procedunt. Ad sextum dicendum quod quis est propter deum non det ipsum elemosine quantum ad esse suum primum tamen dat sibi vltimum complementum secundum quod est meritoria: et ideo vltimo in diffinitione ipsius ponitur. Ad septimum quoniam dicendum quod a peccato desistere non est de essentia satisfactionis: ut ex predictis patet: sed est ad satisfactionem preambulum sicut fundamentum ipsius: unde cum aliquis peccat hoc ipso quod non facit hoc quod facere tenetur: constat quod id quod quis alias facere tenetur non est de essentia satisfactionis sed preambulum ad ipsam: vnde cum ad elemosinarum largitionem quandoque aliquis tenetur quandoque non: ut postea patebit: constat quod illarum elemosinarum largitio ad quas quis tenetur non est pars satisfactionis sed preambulum ad ipsam. Je répondis au Priennois : Mandraïte, je conçois et je partage ton enthousiasme ; il n'y a que le fanatisme de la vertu et de la vérité qui ne soit pas à craindre. Vas ! ton récit ajoute à la vénération que je portais déjà au nom de Thalès. Ton délire est tout naturel, et le sien aussi. On ne fait rien de grand, on n'invente rien de sublime, si l'on n'a pas la mesure de son génie, et le sentiment de ses forces. Thalès a raison d'être jaloux de sa découverte ; elle est son bien ; elle est plus à lui, que les conquêtes de Sémiramis n'étaient à cette femme. On doit tenir à la bonne action dont on a été capable, à une pensée forte et hardie qu'on a su produire. La modestie est la vertu de la médiocrité. Eh ! pourquoi ne pas se rendre justice, et la revendiquer pour soi comme pour les autres ?

Nous nous quittâmes à Myonte, petite ville ionienne, à mi-chemin de Prienne à Milet. C'est là que le Méandre, après tant de détours, tombe enfin dans la mer, et regrette de n'en avoir pas fait encore davantage dans une aussi agréable contrée.

Fatigué du poids de la chaleur, j'allai me réfugier dans un vieux temple entr'ouvert, parce que le néocore le nettoyait en ce moment. Dans le fond du sanctuaire, je distinguai, non sans peine, à cause du peu de jour, la statue assise d'un vieillard, recouvert d'un long manteau fort sale. Son épaule était chargée d'une hache poudreuse.

This digression on the constitution of Boeotia in 395, which is somewhat irrelevant to the account of the factions at Thebes, and still more so to the war between Boeotia and Phocis, is the most valuable section of the papyrus, and disposes of several long debated problems. First, as to the four βουλαί; these were only known from Thuc. v. 38. 2 οἱ Βοιωτάρχαι ἐκοίνωσαν ταῖς τέσσαρσι βουλαῖς τῶν Βοιωτῶν ταῦτα αἵπερ ἅπαν τὸ κῦρος ἔχουσι καὶ παρῄνουν γενέσθαι ὅρκους ταῖς πόλεσιν ὅσαι βούλονται ἐπ’ ὠφελίᾳ σφίσι ξυνομνύναι, and their relation to each other was uncertain, it being often supposed that the four βουλαί corresponded to four different districts. The present passage shows that Köhler (*Sitzungsber. d. Berl. Akad.* 1895, pp. 455-6) was fully justified in connecting them with the four βουλαί which the Athenian oligarchs in 411 proposed to institute εἰς τὸν μέλλοντα χρόνον (Arist. *Ath. Pol.* 30), and each of which was to consist of 100 persons and to hold office for a year in turn; and his conjecture that in the case of important matters, such as treaties, the four Boeotian βουλαί sat together is now completely established. The present passage, however, brings out a new fact of considerable value, that the four βουλαί were not councils of the Boeotian league as a whole, but existed in each of the separate states which formed the federation. Thucydides’ expression ταῖς τέσσαρσι βουλαῖς τῶν Βοιωτῶν is therefore somewhat misleading, since the natural supposition is that he meant βουλαί of the league. There was indeed, in addition to the four βουλαί in the individual states, one federal βουλή for Boeotia (cf. xiii. 12), which met in the Cadmea and consisted of 660 members, contributed by the several states in the proportion of sixty βουλευταί for each Boeotarch, but it is clear that Thucydides is not referring to this; and that the state βουλαί, not the federal βουλή, possessed the supreme authority is indicated by the greater prominence given in P’s account to the former, as well as by Thucydides’ words αἵπερ ἅπαν τὸ κῦρος ἔχουσι, and the circumstance that the treaty in question provisionally made by the Boeotarchs depended for validity on the consent of each individual state, not on a resolution of the federal council. For membership of the state boulai there was a property qualification, so that the numbers of the ruling oligarchies must have varied in the different states, of which there were at least ten (*v. inf.*).

Secondly, as to the number of the Boeotarchs, Thuc. iv. 91 mentions eleven in B.C. 424 τῶν ἄλλων Βοιωταρχῶν οἵ εἰσιν ἕνδεκα οὐ ξυνεπαινούντων μάχεσθαι [...] Παγώνδας ὁ Αἰολάδου Βοιωταρχῶν ἐκ Θηβῶν μετ’ Ἀριανθίδου τοῦ Λυσιμαχίδου κ.τ.λ.; but it was formerly disputed whether or not the figure eleven included the two Theban Boeotarchs. A strong reason for supposing eleven to be the whole number of the Boeotarchs was supplied by Poppo (i. 2, p. 292), namely that if οἵ εἰσιν ἕνδεκα referred to τῶν ἄλλων Βοιωταρχῶν exclusive of the Thebans ἦσαν not εἰσίν should have been written. The number eleven has also been disputed by Wilamowitz (*Hermes*, viii. p. 440), who wished to alter it to seven, corresponding to the seven Boeotian states mentioned in Thuc. iv. 93, a change which has been supported on other grounds and widely accepted e. g. by Cauer, Pauly-Wissowa, *Real-Encycl.* iii. p. 647. Eleven is however the total number of the Boeotarchs in P (xii. 11-20), so that the correctness of the figure in Thuc. iv. 91 is vindicated beyond dispute. It is also noteworthy that P uses ἄρχων merely as a synonym for Boeotarch, and says nothing about an archon of the whole league; this officer therefore, who first appears in third century B.C. inscriptions, is not to be identified with one of the Theban Boeotarchs, as was suggested by Wilamowitz, *l. c.*, still less to be regarded with Freeman (*Hist. of Federal Gov.* i. p. 128) as the most ancient official of the league.

**νομιζόμενα** νόμιμα, ἢ ὑπολαμβανόμενα· Ἀριστοφάνης (Plut. 1186) "οὐκοῦν τὰ νομιζόμενα σὺ τέτων λαμβάνεις." ἐπειδὴ νόμος ἦν τὰ ὑπολειπόμενα τῆς θυσίας τὸν ἱερέα λαμβάνειν. δέρματα καὶ κωλαῖ. cf. v. κωλακρέτης.

**νομοθεσία** θέσις νόμου.

**νομοθέται** τὸ πάλαι Μωυσῆς, μετέπειτα δὲ ὁ Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς.

Et altre Modi discordanti; et de questi ne fa mentione Statio; *Discordesque modos, et singultantia verba Molior.* Ultimamente (lassandone molti altri per breuità) chiamarono in uniuersale alcune compositioni Modi lirici, si come dall'autorità di Ouidio commemorata di sopra si può comprendere. Si trouaua nondimeno grande differenza tra questi Modi: essendo che li popoli di questa prouintia usauano una maniera di Versi, et uno Istrumento; et quelli di quella usauano un'altro Istrumento, et un'altra maniera. Et non erano differenti solamente in questi: ma nelle Harmonie ancora: Imperoche una sorte di harmonia usaua un popolo, et un'altro un'altra; di maniera che erano anco differenti ne i Numeri, i quali si ritrouauano ne i Versi. tius, Italicum. Nunc mitia, undecunque sint allata, cibo non respuuntur. Paulus usum eius commendavit ex aceto et oleo, quod et invitet appetentiam, et lienem laxet, pituitamque per aluum exigat. In officinis nomen retinuit, Vulgus decurtandis nominibus felix, detritis duabus literis, capres quasi cappares profert. Aliqui Latinorum inturim vocant, namque frutex cernitur spinosi generis, in gyrum humi se spargens. Spinas ut rubus habet, in hamum curvatas, folia cotonei, fructum olivae, quo dehiscente flos candidus erumpit, quo deciduo, glans oblonga coalescit, quae demum se pandens acinulos repraesentat rubentes, quales in punico malo spectantur, radicibus furculosis grandibus. Cauliculi, folia, flores, femina, glandes sale conditae deferuntur ad nos hac specie et figura quam diximus. Fruticem iam alit Gallia. In Cypro capparis plurimum provenit. Parum alimoniae vescentibus praebet, quod partium tenuitate polleat, medicinae potius quam cibo nascens. Fructus sale conspersus adservatur, alioqui cito corruptionem sentit. Recens salem non expertus plus alit quam eodem inveteratus, aluum tamen magis movet. Elutus et tantisper maceratus dum omnem salis naturam deponat, minime quidem enutrit, sed elanguescentem appetentiam invitat. Fastidia ciborum discutit, pituitam quae in ventre coierat deijcit, lienis ac iocineris obstruentes inferctus expedit. Verum ad hos usus praestandos, ex aceto mulso, aut oleo et aceto caeteris dapibus praeponi debet. Teneris germinibus dum virent cum aceto et sale vescuntur, atque ad usus recondunt. Ferunt eos qui quotidie edunt resolutione nervorum non periclitari, nec lienis doloribus. Radix vitiligines albas tollit, si trita in sole fricentur. Spleneticis prodest in vino pota, radicis cortex duabus drachmis, dempto balnearum usu. Feruntque, triginta quinque diebus per urinam et aluum, totum lienem emitti. Bibitur in lumborum doloribus, ac paralysi. Dentium dolores sedat tritum ex aceto semen decoctum, uel manducata radix. Infunditur aurium dolori decoctum oleo. Ulcera quae phagedenas vocant, folia et radix recens cum melle sanat. sic et strumas, et parotidas discutit radix. Oris exulcerationes in aceto decocta tollit: iocineris quoque malis medetur, vermiculos aurium necat. Dant ad tineas in aceto et melle. Stomacho inutiles esse inter authores convenit. Caulis et fructus cibi gratia condiuntur. Aluum conturbat, stomacho officit, sitim creat. Cocta tamen stomacho quam cruda utilior est. Semen ipsum duabus drachmis in vino haustis per quadraginta dies lienem absumit. Urinas trahit, cruentaque strigmenta pellit. Prodest in coxendicum doloribus et nervorum resolutione: item ruptis et convulsis. Menses ciet, capitis pituitam elicit. Dentium dolores sedat semen ex aceto decoctum si colluatur os. Eofdem habet effectus cortex radicis aridus. Ulcera omnia vetusta et sordida et quae occalluerunt expurgat. Lienosis cum farina hordei linitur. Radix mordicus apprehensa dente malum id levat. Vitiligines candidas tollit cum aceto trito. Radix et folia intrita strumas ac duritias discutiunt. Contra vermiculos aurium fuccus infunditur. Peregrinum cappari quod e Marmarica Libye deportatur, magnas excitat inflationes. Apulum vomitus ciet. Asperrimum Africum, et quod e mari rubro convehitur. siquidem in ore pustulas attollit, inimicum gingiuis, eas enim osse tenus exest, quare cibis damnatum.

Lepidi facies a Dioscoride non repraesentatur. Peregrinum olim fuit lepidium, nunc multis in locis seritur a Fauonio: dein cum fruticaverit, iuxta terrae praeciditur, et velut porrum sectiuum demetitur, sed rarius. Post Calendas Novembres secandum non erit, quoniam frigoribus violatum emoritur, praesertim si seuitia hyemis ingrauat, nam impatientissimum est algoris: biennio tamen sufficiet, si diligenter sarritum runcetur, et stercore satietur. Multis in locis vivacitatem suam usque ad annos decem prorogat. Exit, ut Plinius tradit, in cubitalem altitudinem, foliis laurinis, sed mollibus. Usus eius non sine lacte. Paulus Aegineta volumine tertio in Ischiadis mentione ait, Lepidium quod apud nos nascitur, fruticosum est, foliis lauri, longe maiorib. aestate sunt efficaciora. Quae si tempus anni negauerit, cortice radicis uti frondium vice conveniet. Miram ischiadicis et longis valetudinibus dedit experientiam. Nonus locus est per quem cum aliis quae constant esse peccata: hoc de quo quaestio est comparatur: et ita per contentionem quanto atrocius et indignius sit id de quo agitur ostenditur. Decimus locus est per quem omnia quae in negocio gerendo acta sunt quaeque post negocium consecuta sunt cum uniuscuiusque indignatione et criminatione colligimus et res uerbis quam maxime ante oculos eius apud quem dicitur ponimus: ut id indignum est perinde illi uideatur indignum: ac si ipse interfuerit: ac praesens uiderit. Undecimus locus est per quem ostendimus ab eo factum in quo minime oportuerit: et a quo si alius faceret prohiberi conueniret. Duodecimus locus est per quem indignamur: quod nobis hoc primum acciderit: nec alicui unquam usu euenerit. Terciusdecimus locus est si cum iniuria contumelia iuncta demonstratur per quem locum in superbiam et arrogantiam odium incitatur. Quartusdecimus locus est per quem petimus ab his qui audiunt ut ad suas res nostras iniurias referant si ad pueros pertinebit de liberis suis cogitet si ad mulieres de uxoribus si ad senes de parentibus aut patribus. Quintusdecimus locus est: per quem dicimus inimicis quoque et hostibus ea quae nobis acciderint: indigna uideri solere et indignatio quae his fere de locis grauissime sumetur. Sum pauper, æger, senex, iam orbatus filio optimo, optimæ spei, adolescente mei amantissimo, per iniuriam: alter, cum modica atque exigua admodum spe bonæ fortunæ, propagandæ stirpis, filia, iam nono anno nupta, sterilis. Ego alias omnibus modis florens, amicitia, filiis, lucris, bona valetudine: iuvenis in magnam spem erectus, assuetus non solum commodis, sed etiam deliciis: nunc vero totus ærumnosus, despectus, multis cum inimicis, non solum infelicem esse existimo, sed quam unquam alias ante feliciorem longe. Neque insanio, neque glorior, actiones id ostendunt: constantissimo animo profiteor, ac ob id etiam frequentissimum est auditorium: omnia administro melius quam antea: scripta quæ nuper confeci, si quis prioribus conferat, intelliget pleniorem, vividiorem, purioremque mihi mentem inesse. At tu, quicunque es, ob unum infortunium, etiam levissimum, muliebriter eiulas: nos tot & tanta ferimus: hoc unum lucrati, ut nec pigeat vitæ ob virtutem & scientiam: nec timeamus mortem, finem tot periculorum atque incommodorum, remque adeo necessariam: alius ex calamitate, quæ etiam calamitas non est, longe magis discruciatur: & quod per incuriam famuli equus claudicet, exclamat, noctes insomnes ducit, tot ansæ felicitatis nullum solamen illi adducunt, tanquam totus sit in sui equi pede: miser est alius quia contemnitur, alius quoniam filius illi nepos, alius quia de uxoris pudicitia timet, alius quia excidit a Magistratu, tentat laqueo vitam finire. Ergo sensus hominum & gustus delicatiores, tum ignorantia rerum & conditionis nostræ, ac desperatio futuræ vitæ, homines reddunt miseros, etiam minimis ex causis: adeo ut huiusmodi homines non possint ulla ratione esse felices, nec in adversis possint consolari. Vide qualis sit vita nostra. Duo sunt homines, quorum uterque perpetuis sex mensibus (ut de muribus Alpinis referunt) dormit: horum unus somniat carceres, vincula cruces, laqueos, tormenta, cædes filiorum, metus, excidia, fugas, tempestates, morbos, inopiam, famem: modo solus vectatur in vadabundo mari, spe salutis posita: modo per deserta, omnium inops, fugit equites tyranni: modo vincitur, & in tetrum barathrum coniicitur: alias ducitur ad supplicium: modo a turba ut insanus exsibilatur. Contra alter somniat regna, honores, epulas, ludos, societates, viridaria, arces, itinera iucunda, scorta, uxorem pulchram, filios, atque ex una voluptate in alteram transit. Quin etiam non contentus his humanis deliciis, fertur ad cælum, videt pulcherrima, gloriosa, & supra fidem: modo rapitur ad spectacula, ad Musicorum egregiorum certamen, ad vireta, venationesque aucupia, piscationes. Inde ambo simul expergiscuntur: quis tam stultus est, ut hunc felicem, illum alium infelicem esse dicat? At hoc (respondebis) somnium est breve, minus afficit, nihil ex illo aliis relinquitur: vita vero sit longior cum vero rerum sensu, maioreque voluptate atque dolore, ex qua dum eximus, remanent illa aliis: filij, offines, opes, non omnino ut in somnio evanescunt. Nugaris: tempus hoc sex mensium felicitatis perpetuæ, primum si quis recte consideret, in quantacunque vita longa, nemo æquat. De sensu, curis, voluptate, omnia in somnis maiora & sunt & videntur quam in vigilia: idque etiam ratio suadet, cum a sensibus tamen non distrahamur. At quod ad veram vitam spectat, hoc est quod contendimus: verum intervallum inter futuram vitam & hanc longe maius est, quam inter vigiliam & somnum. Quæ vero relinquuntur, si ad stultam spem referantur, aliquid sunt: atque ob id magis dolendum quod relinquere cogamur: si ad veram opinionem, si ad successus rerum respicimus, falsa imagine decipimur. Ita cuilibet fingere licet immortalem vitam, regnum immensum atque pacatum: sed quæ nugæ res moveri non possunt: ita statuere oportet de vita nostra, ut vere sit somnium. At, ut dixi, si maius aliquid fuisset, eo rem meam evexeram, ut ex infelicissimo felicissimus dici possem: & ex pauperrimo, mea & filij opera ad duo millia coronatorum aureorum in singulos annos lucraremur: nullius ordinis homines, nulli Principes nostris in manibus non essent. Viceram invidiam, superaveram æmulationem, contuderam conspirationes, in intima penetraveram: aperueram vias, struxeram mihi aditum ad omnia & mihi & filio. Quin etiam Principum occasio extenorum non magis quam alij cuiquam defuit. Primum quidem apud Dacorum Regem, inde Gallorum, mox etiam ad Scotos vocatus fui. ### CAPVT IIII.
->Erkennung von Stichen/ Pfeilschuß/ Fäll und Knütschung.<-

<margin>A</margin>Nun weiter von andern geschlechten der Wunden/ als von Stich/ Pfeilschuß/ Fäll/ und dergleichen. Zwischen diesen und den Wunden ist kein underscheid irs wesens/ als allein in dem/ daß ein solcher Stich/ oder Pfeil dem Anfall seiner Enge halben/ nicht mag statt geben/ darumb er weiter in das Fleisch und Adern gehet/ dann ein Wunden. Dann es ist eines jeglichen Anfalls art/ daß er vil Höle umb sich haben wil/ und Weite. Darumb die offnen Wunden/ so nit verhefft/ mit weniger Anfalls und Sorgen beladen seind als die verhefften. Und je mehr ein Wunden oben zusammen getrungẽ wird/ je sorglicher sie unden am Boden ist. Also ist es mit den Stichen und Pfeilschuß/ so sie aussen verschwellen/ der Anfall einwärts dringt/ denselbigen Lacerten/ meatibus und Adern nach: Darumb sie mehr zum todt und sorglicher als offen Wunden/ so außwendig weit sind.

Auch ist in solchem zu mercken/ daß ein Stich oder Pfeil von stund an soll außgezogen werden/ ehe daß die Geschwulst und Anfall zugehet. Wo solches aber nit geschicht/ mehr zum Tod ist/ dann zum Leben. Und wo solche sorg vor Augen were/ mit genugsamen Zeichen/ da soll dasselbig Instrument inen bleiben/ und lassen durch die Mumia herauß gehen. Dann sein Heylung hat ein andern Griff/ und das in zween wege: Der ein/ daß ein Wunden neben Pfeil gehawe werde/ oder durch den Mumia, der zu attrahiren gemischt ist/ außgezogen/ unnd nit von der Hand. Was also die Arzney außzeucht/ das ist dem Leben nit nachtheilig. Also ist es auch mit den Knütschen oder Fall/ daß am selbigen ort auch Wunden gemacht werden/ auch daß der Anfall ein außgang habe/ und nit ihn hinweg nach dem Leben gehe/ Oder durch den Mumia außwendig gestillet und vertriben. Dann an ein jeglichen: Stoß oder Knütschung/ sey wie hart und streng es wölle/ blau oder schwartz/ so vermags der Mumia in sein erst Wesen zubringen/ ohn Auffschneidung oder Eyterung. Wann solche Inflationes seind nit zerbrechung/ oder von zerbrochner Natur/ sonder ein Geschwulst in guten dingen/ Darumb sie also hingehn/ ohn weiter Zufall.

<margin>B</margin>So sichs aber begebe/ daß ein Fall/ Stich/ oder dergleichen in die inwendigen regiones gangen were/ Adern/ oder etwas gebrochen hette dadurch den regionibus ein frembder Gast zu fiel: Am selbigen ort soltu geflissen sein/ solches zuvertreibe/ wie von den Zufällen geschrieben wird/ Aber so ein solch Eisen sich anglettet/ oder widerhecket/ da wisse/ daß es hindersich nit außgehet/ sonder durchgestossen soll werden: Oder aber in ein Geschwer gebracht/ und herauß gefeilt/ so dieselbige statt dem Leben nit nachtheilig were. Aber ob solchs fürgenommen werde/ mit Mumia attractiva verbunden/ welcher die Geschwulst dermassen niderlegt/ und den Anfall nimpt/ daß der Hacken wider zuruck gehet den weg/ da er hin ist gangen. Du solt auch gewarnet sein/ daß du in keinem wege mit Zangen oder Instrumenten dich understehest etwas zumachen. Dann du äffelst das Glied: Es were dann so nahe bey der Haut/ oder an ein flachen ort/ da es ohn sorg anzunemen were: Wiewol ohn Mumia ist es selten möglich. Dergleichen auch begibt sich vil/ dz Kuglen also in Leib geschossen werden/ und durch den Mumiam attractivam, durch sein art und natur/ widerumb herauß gezogen werden: Es were dann sach/ daß die Kugel in ein ander Region fiele. Darinn merck/ daß der Mumia in frembden regionibus nit gewalt hat: darumb so ein Kugel geschossen wird in Leib/ und fiele zwischen die Intestina nider/ oder käme ausserhalb oder underhalb dem Diaphragma, am selben ort ist es nicht möglich herauß zuziehen. Dergleichen/ so in ein Röhre geschossen wird/ und die Kugel suncke im Rohr undersich/ so ists auch ein ander Region. Und ob schon der Mumia so starck were/ die Kuglen herauß zuziehen/ so gibts die Rewe/ so inwendig am Rohr ist/ nit zu. Darumb in solchen stücken gut acht zu haben ist/ war mit einer umbgehe.

### CAPVT V.
->Von Heylung der obgemelten/ und was darzu gehört.<-

<margin>C</margin>Nun ist die Heylung solcher Wunden/ gleich dem Proceß von gemeinen Wunden: Scheidt sich allein in dem/ daß der Mumia soll mit attractivis gespeist sein/ unnd sollen attractiva sein/ die da nicht humores an sich ziehen/ noch liquores, oder dergleichen/ sonder allein/ das sie Metallen/ Holz oder Bein/ etc. annemen: Wann solten die gemeinen attractiva gebraucht werden/ so stünden Flüß hinzu.

Wiewol es sich auch manchmal begibt/ daß ein Kugel oder solch Eisen/ in den lacertis verheylen/ auß ursach des guten Mumia, der in kein Anfall gefallen ist/ oder nit starck erzörnt ist worden. Etwann nach vil jaren mit der zeit sich eytet und wider außfelt: Solchs wird der Natur zugelassen/ und nit understanden zunemen. Dann so es die Natur verheylet/ wer wils ihr wider nemen?

Von den attractivis zureden/ seind etliche die Holz ziehen/ Fäsen und solch ding/ als Asphaltum und Carabæ: Etliche Eisen/ als Magnes: Etlich Kupffer und Zinn/ als die gefärbten Amethisten: Etlich Bley unnd Stein/ als der Alabaster. Etlich Lympen vom Fleische/ Beinschröt/ als die Gummi/ Terpentin/ unnd Asphaltum. Etlich in allen stücken/ als die Serpentina. Wie solche Krafft all seind/ soll von eim Artzet nicht gescheiden sein. Wann in wirckung der Natur/ so sie den Wunden ubergelegt werden/ attrahierens alle gleich/ also/ was hauffen Stroh und Holz zeucht/ das zeucht in Wunden Eisen/ Bley/ Stein/ und Beyn: Hinwiderumb auch/ was allein Eisen zeucht das zeucht in Wunden was ledig darinn ligt. Darumb ein Artzt nit soll den außwendigen kräfften nachgehen/ sondern den inwendigen/ wie sie sich mit der Natur vereinigen.

كان رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، يبرز بنفسه للمطر إذا نزل ويكشف رأسه له حتى يصيب منه ويقول: إنه حديث عهد بربه. فانظر إلى هذه المعرفة بالله من هذا النبي ما أجلها وما أعلاها وأوضحها. فقد سخر المطر أفضل البشر لقربه من ربه فكان مثل الرسول الذي ينزل بالوحي عليه، فدعاه بالحال بذاته فبرز إليه ليصيب منه ما أتاه به من ربه فلو لا ما حصلت له منه <gloss>١</gloss> الفائدة الإلهية بما أصاب منه، ما برز بنفسه إليه. فهذه رسالة ماء جعل الله منه ﴿كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ (الأنبياء: ٣٠) فافهم.

وأما حكمة إلقائه في التابوت ورميه في اليم، فالتابوت ناسوته، واليم ما حصل له من العلم بواسطة هذا الجسم مما أعطته القوة النظرية الفكرية والقوى الحسية والخيالية التي لا يكون شيء منها ولا من أمثالها لهذه <gloss>٢</gloss> النفس الإنسانية إلا بوجود [١٣٨ الف] هذا الجسم العنصري. فلما حصلت النفس في هذا الجسم وأمرت بالتصرف فيه وتدبيره، جعل الله لها هذه القوى آلات <gloss>٣</gloss> يتوصل بها إلى ما أراده الله منها في تدبير هذا التابوت الذي فيه سكينة الرب.

فرمى به في اليم ليحصل بهذه القوى على فنون العلم فأعلمه بذلك أنه وإن كان الروح المدبر له هو الملك، فإنه لا يدبره إلا به. فأصحبه هذه القوى الكائنة في هذا الناسوت الذي عبر عنه بالتابوت في باب الإشارات والحكم.

كذلك تدبير الحق العالم ما دبره إلا به أو بصورته، فما دبره إلا به كتوقف الولد على إيجاد الوالد، والمسببات على أسبابها، والمشروطات على شروطها، والمعلولات على عللها، والمدلولات على أدلتها، والمحققات على حقائقها. وكل ذلك من العالم وهو تدبير الحق فيه. فما دبره إلا به. وأما قولنا أو بصورته، أعنى صورة العالم، فأعنى به الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى التي تسمى الحق بها واتصف بها. فما وصل إلينا اسم تسمى به إلا وجدنا معنى ذلك الاسم وروحه في العالم. فما دبر العالم أيضا إلا بصورة العالم.

ولذلك قال في خلق آدم الذي هو البرنامج الجامع لنعوت الحضرة الإلهية التي هي الذات والصفات والأفعال: «إن الله خلق آدم على صورته.» وليست صورته سوى الحضرة الإلهية. فأوجد <gloss>٤</gloss> في هذا المختصر الشريف الذي هو الإنسان الكامل جميع الأسماء الإلهية وحقائق ما خرج عنه في العالم الكبير المنفصل، وجعله روحا

( तीसरा हेतु ) अपनी जातिमें अवस्थित रहनेसे भी ( द्रव्य ) प्रधान है जैसे जो पार्थिव द्रव्य है वह सब अवस्था में पार्थिवही रहता है अन्यभावको प्राप्त नहीं होता ( अर्थात् जो पार्थिव द्रव्य है वह पार्थिव ही रहता है और कभी आप्य, तैजस आदि नहीं होता ) इसी प्रकार शेष आप्य, तैजस, वायवीय और नाभस आदिको जानना कि ये भी अपनी २ जातिसे पृथक् नहीं होते ॥ ३ ॥ ( चौथा हेतु ) पांचों इन्द्रियोंद्वारा ग्रहण होनेसे भी ( द्रव्यही ) प्रधान है क्योंकि द्रव्यही पांचों इंद्रियों ( श्रोत्र, त्वचा, नेत्र, जिह्वा और घ्राण ) इनसे ग्रहण किया जा सकता है । और रसादिक पांचों इंद्रियोंसे ग्रहण नहीं किये जा सकते ( केवल एक रसना इंद्रियसे रसका ग्रहण होता है इत्यादि ) ॥ ४ ॥ ( पांचवां हेतु ) द्रव्य सब रसादिका आश्रय स्थान होनेसे भी ( द्रव्य ) प्रधान है कि द्रव्य स्वतंत्र है और रस गुण वीर्य विपाकादि सब द्रव्यके आश्रयभूत ( अधीन ) हैं ॥ ५ ॥

"आरंभसामर्थ्याच्च" द्रव्याश्रित आरंभो यथा विदारिगन्धादिकमाहृत्य संक्षुद्य विपचेदित्येवमादिषु न रसादिष्वारंभः ॥ ६ ॥
"शास्त्रप्रामाण्याच्च" शास्त्रे हि द्रव्यं प्रधानमुपदेशे हि योगानां यथा मातुलुंगाग्निमंथौ चेति न रसाद्य उपदिश्यंते ॥ ७ ॥

( छठा हेतु ) द्रव्यमें आरम्भका सामर्थ्य होनेसे भी ( द्रव्य ) प्रधान है क्योंकि क्रियाका आरंभ द्रव्यके आश्रय ( अर्थात् आधीन ) है । जैसे विदारीगंधा ( शालपर्णी ) आदिको लाकर कूटे और फिर पकावे इत्यादि सब क्रियाओंका आरंभ द्रव्यमेंही होता है रसादिकमें किसी क्रियाकाभी आरम्भ नहीं हो सकता ॥ ६ ॥
( सातवां हेतु ) शास्त्रके प्रमाणोंसे भी ( द्रव्य ) प्रधान है क्योंकि शास्त्रमें भी द्रव्यही प्रधान माना गया है । जैसे योगों ( नुसखों ) के उपदेशमें मातुलुंग ( नींबू ) तथा अग्निमंथ ( अरनी ) इत्यादि द्रव्योंहीका उपदेश किया गया है कुछ रसादिका उपदेश कहीं किसी योगमें प्रायः नहीं किया ॥ ७ ॥
